text: When an ECP5 IIR is stuck at 28.7 MHz because the critical loop runs unregistered through a MULT18X18D and a 25-cell state carry chain, cut state_width from 24 to 18 and switch dsp_regs to in_pipe_out with pipe_mul=1, which shortens the carry chain and registers the multiplier out of the loop, giving 38.3 MHz (+9.5 MHz) and -33 LUTs.

On ECP5 IIR, when Fmax is limited by a 21-cell fabric carry chain (u_s1.x, 2.31 ns logic + 2.55 ns route) into a LUT4, avoid adding both DSP in_pipe and out registers—it only moves 38.27→38.91 MHz (+0.6 MHz, neutral, 526 LUT/8 DSP) because the critical path stays the fabric carry/LUT, so shorten the carry chain or state width instead.

When an ECP5 IIR is limited by a 24-bit state carry chain and unregistered DSP feed-forward/recursive path, do not shorten state_width to 20 with dsp_regs=out,in_pipe_out expecting Fmax: it saved 10 LUTs but the critical path merely moved to the 20-cell u_s1.ra2 carry chain and total delay rose 25.7→26.27 ns, dropping Fmax 38.9→38.1 MHz (-0.8), so keep the state headroom or register the DSP loop instead.

When an ECP5 IIR recursive loop is timing-limited by a 20-cell carry chain in the state accumulator, cut state width from 20 to 18 and remove DSP input/feed-forward registers to shorten the critical path from 26.27 to 25.56 ns (carry chain 20->11 cells), gaining only +1.07 MHz (38.06->39.13 MHz) at +10 LUTs without reaching 40 MHz, because the recursive DSP route still dominates.

When an ECP5 IIR is timing-limited at 39.1 MHz by a 25.56 ns recursive DSP loop, keep the per-section b-multiplier output register rather than deleting it to relieve placement pressure, because removing it puts the 3.93 ns MULT18X18D directly in the s1->y->a1*y->s1 path and drops Fmax by 10.9 MHz to 28.2 MHz while saving only 16 LUTs.

On an ECP5 IIR whose DSP recursive loop is timing-limited by the FF→MULT18X18D→carry-chain path, enable the DSP output register and remove the pre-DSP input register to cut the critical path from 35.4 ns to 26.1 ns and raise Fmax from 28.2 to 38.4 MHz (+10.2 MHz) for +16 LUTs and no extra DSPs by keeping the multiplier delay off the recursive accumulator loop.

When an ECP5 IIR is timing-limited at 38.4 MHz by the recursive a-multiplier loop (DSP plus two ~21-cell carry chains), don't spend both DSP input and output registers on the feed-forward b multipliers—it only moves Fmax to 38.9 MHz with LUT/DSP unchanged at 526/8 because the recursive loop remains the critical path.

When an ECP5 IIR is DSP-combinational timing-limited at 40.1 MHz by a MULT18X18D feeding a carry chain, enable the DSP output register to remove the multiplier's 5.3 ns logic+route delay from that path, raising Fmax by 12.6 MHz to 52.7 MHz with no LUT/DSP change even though it remains infeasible.

When an ECP5 IIR is timing-flat at 52.7 MHz on an 18-cell carry chain (u_s1.ra1) rather than the DSP, don't add multiplier pipelining or remove DSP output registers—they gave 0 MHz delta and identical 284 LUT/8 DSP—instead retime or restructure the carry-chain adder.

When an ECP5 IIR is DSP-combinational timing-limited with the DSP output unregistered, sweep pipe_mul=1 with dsp_regs='out' to register the DSP output; it shortens the critical path from 18.97 ns (u_s1.ra1 carry chain) to 18.32 ns (u_s1.x), raising Fmax 52.7→54.6 MHz with LUT 284 and DSP 8 unchanged.
